title: ZoomInfo Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Add-Ons
summary: ZoomInfo pricing varies by tier—Professional, Advanced, and Elite—but upfront rates aren't published.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits ZoomInfo buyers hit


Before you accept the quote, check that it lists four things beyond the plan name.


The four are how many credits you get and what overage costs, what the contract does at renewal, which modules are billed separately, and which integrations your tier includes.


Those are the lines your competing quote has to match, so check each one: the annual credit cap and overage rate, the export limits (which ZoomInfo doesn't publish), the auto-renewal terms, the renewal price uplift (which buyers report anecdotally), the add-on modules, the integrations gated by tier, and any onboarding fees.


Ask the rep to point to the contract clause for each, and write down the date you checked it. Terms change, and a quote from last spring tells you little about this renewal.


### ZoomInfo credit and export caps


If a team burns through its allotment early, the choice is to stop pulling contacts or pay overage at whatever rate the contract sets, because credits are the meter on your usage.


Ask for that rate in writing before you sign. Because the export limit isn't published, you only learn it by asking, and a limit you discover mid-quarter is one you can't plan around.


Unless you give notice within a window, most contracts renew on their own. Miss it and you owe another term, often at a higher price. Buyers report uplifts at renewal, so treat the first-year price as an introduction and ask for the renewal price now.


You may assume features such as extra data types or workflow tools are part of the plan, but they can be separate modules with their own line on the invoice.


Name the work your team does every week and ask whether each task is in the plan or costs extra.


Whether ZoomInfo connects to your customer database or sales tools may depend on your tier. If the connection is the point of buying, confirm your tier includes it. Otherwise your team ends up exporting by hand, and that runs straight into the export limit.
